fl-q1.text: Classify the leak (para 2-14). Wipe the area clean and watch it. Which class is it?

options.label: Class I — wetness or discoloration, no drops form
Class II — drops form but do not drip from the item
Class III — drops drip/fall from the item

fl-q2.text: What is leaking? (The LMTV service brakes are air-operated; there is no brake-fluid reservoir to check.)

options.label: Engine oil, transmission oil, hydraulic/power steering oil, or coolant
Engine oil, transmission oil, hydraulic/power steering oil, or coolant

fl-t1.text: Class I/II leakage is allowed (para 2-14). Check the fluid level of the leaking item often and keep it at the proper level. When in doubt, notify Unit Maintenance.

terminal.summary: Class I/II leak (oil/coolant/hydraulic) — within limits, monitor fluid level

fl-t2.text: Class I/II fuel seepage is allowed by para 2-14, but keep it away from heat and ignition sources, check it often, and report it to Unit Maintenance. If it gets worse to dripping (Class III), the vehicle is NMC.

terminal.summary: Class I/II fuel leak — allowed, monitor and report

fl-t3.text: Class III leak. Do not operate — report to Unit Maintenance (para 2-14; PMCS NMC criterion "Class III leak is evident").

terminal.summary: Class III fluid leak — NMC, report to Unit Maintenance

fl-t4.text: Class III fuel leak — fire hazard. Do not operate. Report to Unit Maintenance immediately.

terminal.summary: Class III fuel leak — NMC, fire hazard

td-q1.text: What is wrong with the tire or wheel?

options.label: Cut, gouge, or crack to the cord body, or an unusual bulge
Tread worn to the wear bar (1/8 in. / 3 mm or less)
Pressure low or not right for the CTIS mode
Lug nuts or studs loose, missing, or broken / wheel wobbles

td-t1.text: A missing or deflated tire is NMC (PMCS item 38). Notify Unit Maintenance; change the tire only if directed (para 3-5).

terminal.summary: Tire flat/deflated or missing — NMC

td-t2.text: A cut, gouge, or crack that extends to the cord body, or an unusual bulge, is NMC (PMCS item 46a).

terminal.summary: Tire cut/gouge/crack to cord body or bulge — NMC

td-t3.text: Tread worn to the height of the tread bar is NMC (PMCS items 38/46a).

terminal.summary: Tire worn to wear bar — NMC

td-a1.text: Select the correct CTIS mode and check pressures
td-a1.actionText: Start the engine and select the CTIS mode for the terrain (para 2-23). Check each tire with a tire gage: HWY 55 psi, X-C 33 psi, SAND 20 psi, EMER 14 psi (±3 psi).

td-q2.text: Do the tires inflate and hold the correct pressure?

options.label: No — a tire will not hold air
No — pressures are off but the tires hold air

terminal.summary: Low tire pressure — corrected with CTIS

td-t6.text: Tire pressures are not within ±3 psi of the CTIS setting. Notify Unit Maintenance (PMCS item 46d).

terminal.summary: CTIS tire pressures out of tolerance — notify Unit Maintenance

td-t5.text: A cracked, broken, or bent wheel is NMC (PMCS item 46b).

terminal.summary: Wheel cracked/broken/bent — NMC

td-q3.text: Check the wheel studs and lug nuts on that wheel (k2). What do you find?

options.label: Two or more nuts or studs missing, loose, or broken on the same wheel
All tight and present, but the wheel still wobbles

td-t7.text: Two or more nuts or studs missing, loose, or broken on the same wheel is NMC (PMCS item 46c). Notify Unit Maintenance.

terminal.summary: Two or more lug nuts/studs missing, loose, or broken — NMC

td-t8.text: Loose lug nut tightened. WARNING: notify Unit Maintenance that lug nuts need to be torqued to 415-475 lb-ft (563-644 N·m) as soon as possible (k2).

terminal.summary: Loose lug nut tightened — Unit Maintenance to torque

td-t9.text: Wheel wobbles or shimmies with no loose or missing nuts. Notify Unit Maintenance (k2).

terminal.summary: Wheel wobbles/shimmies — notify Unit Maintenance

td-a2.text: Check tire pressures for each CTIS setting
td-a2.actionText: Check each tire with a tire gage for each CTIS setting (HWY 55, X-C 33, SAND 20, EMER 14 psi). Notify Unit Maintenance if pressures do not match (k1).

td-t10.text: Tires wear unevenly or excessively. Notify Unit Maintenance (k1).

terminal.summary: Uneven or excessive tire wear — notify Unit Maintenance

ws-q1.text: What happens when you try to start?

options.label: Engine does not crank at all
Engine cranks but does not start

ws-q2.text: Open the battery box (para 3-8a). Are the battery cables damaged, or are the cables or terminal posts corroded?

options.label: No — cables and posts look good

ws-t1.text: Do not clean or repair the battery cables yourself — the TM says notify Unit Maintenance for corroded or damaged cables/posts (a1).

terminal.summary: Engine will not crank — battery cables/posts corroded or damaged

ws-q3.text: Check the battery fluid level (para 3-8b). Is it low?

ws-t2.text: Low battery fluid: notify Unit Maintenance (a1, PMCS item 48c). Close the battery box (para 3-8c).

terminal.summary: Engine will not crank — battery fluid low

ws-q4.text: Close the battery box (para 3-8c). Turn the main light switch to SER DRIVE (para 2-21c). Do the service lights come on?

ws-q5.text: Remove the PDP cover (para 3-13a). Is circuit breaker CB70 tripped?

ws-a1.actionText: Push CB70 in to reset it. Turn the main light switch to SER DRIVE and check the service lights, then try to start (para 2-21a or b). Install the PDP cover (para 3-13b).

ws-q5a.text: Do the lights work and does the engine crank now?

ws-t3.text: 12/24 VDC circuits do not operate. Notify Unit Maintenance (e2).

terminal.summary: Engine will not crank — 12/24 VDC circuits inoperative

ws-t4.text: CB70 was tripped; reset restored power and the engine cranks.

terminal.summary: CB70 tripped — reset, engine cranks

ws-q6.text: Master power switch ON, windshield wiper switch to "I". Do the wipers operate?

ws-t5.text: 24 VDC circuits do not operate. Notify Unit Maintenance (e3).

terminal.summary: Engine will not crank — 24 VDC circuits inoperative

ws-q7.text: Look at the WTEC II TEPSS / WTEC III TPSS. What does it show?

options.label: Another range — I pressed N and it went to N
Will not go into N, beeps, or shows "--"

ws-q7a.text: Try to start again (para 2-21a or b). Does the engine crank now?

ws-t7.text: Transmission was not in neutral. Selected N and the engine cranks.

terminal.summary: Transmission not in N — selected N, engine cranks

ws-a2.text: Check the shift selector circuit breakers (f4)
ws-a2.actionText: Master power OFF. Remove the PDP cover (para 3-13a). If CB43 or CB79 (or CB35 on WTEC II) is tripped, push it in. Master power ON and check whether it trips again. Install the PDP cover (para 3-13b).

ws-q7b.text: Does the shift selector light up and show N, and does the engine crank?

options.label: No, or a breaker trips again

ws-t8.text: Shift selector breaker was tripped; reset and the engine cranks.

terminal.summary: Shift selector circuit breaker reset — engine cranks

ws-t6.text: Transmission shift selector fault. Notify Unit Maintenance (f1/f3/f4; PMCS item 20).

terminal.summary: Engine will not crank — transmission shift selector fault

ws-q9.text: Remove the PDP cover (para 3-13a). Is CB21 or CB77 tripped?

ws-a3.actionText: Push the tripped breaker in to reset. Attempt to start the engine (para 2-21a or b). Install the PDP cover (para 3-13b).

options.label: No, or a breaker tripped again

ws-t10.text: CB21/CB77 was tripped; reset and the engine cranks.

terminal.summary: CB21/CB77 tripped — reset, engine cranks

ws-t9.text: Engine does not crank after operator checks. Notify Unit Maintenance (e1).

terminal.summary: Engine will not crank — needs maintenance

ws-q8.text: Master power ON (para 2-21a or b). Does the FUEL gage read at or below E?

ws-a4.actionText: WARNING: no smoking or open flame; engine off. Fuel the vehicle (para 2-20a), then prime the fuel/water separator (next step).

ws-a5.actionText: Raise the cab (para 2-22a). Depress the button on the fuel/water separator as many times as necessary until the button is tight. Lower the cab (para 2-22b). Attempt to start the engine (para 2-21a or b).

ws-q10.text: Does the engine start and keep running?

ws-t11.text: Engine starts after fueling/priming the fuel/water separator.

terminal.summary: Out of fuel / fuel system not primed — corrected, engine runs

ws-t12.text: Engine cranks but does not start (or stalls) after fueling and priming. Notify Unit Maintenance (a2/b1/e5).

terminal.summary: Engine cranks but will not start — needs maintenance

options.label: Nothing electrical works (no lights, no gages)
A gage reads wrong or does not work
Headlights, turn signals, stoplights, or taillights
Batteries will not stay charged / VOLTS gage out of range

el-q2.text: Remove the PDP cover (para 3-13a). Is circuit breaker CB70 tripped?

el-a1.actionText: Push CB70 in to reset. Turn the main light switch to SER DRIVE (para 2-21c) and check the service lights. Install the PDP cover (para 3-13b).

el-q3.text: Do the service lights work now?

el-t1.text: CB70 was tripped; reset and circuits restored.

terminal.summary: CB70 tripped — reset, circuits restored

el-t2.text: 12/24 VDC circuits do not operate. Notify Unit Maintenance (e2).

terminal.summary: 12/24 VDC circuits inoperative — needs maintenance

options.label: OIL PRESS or FRONT/REAR BRAKE AIR gage

el-a2.text: Fill the tank and check CB77
el-a2.actionText: Fill the fuel tank — if the FUEL gage shows less than full, notify Unit Maintenance. Remove the PDP cover; master power OFF; if CB77 is tripped push it in; master power ON and see if it trips again. Install the PDP cover (e6).

el-t3.text: FUEL gage does not operate or is inaccurate. Notify Unit Maintenance if it still does not work (e6). The FUEL gage check (PMCS item 18) has no NMC criterion.

terminal.summary: FUEL gage inoperative/inaccurate — notify Unit Maintenance

el-q5.text: Master power OFF. Remove the PDP cover (para 3-13a). Is CB77 tripped?

el-a3.actionText: Push CB77 in. Master power ON and check whether it trips again. Install the PDP cover (para 3-13b).

el-q6.text: Does the gage work correctly now?

el-t6.text: CB77 was tripped; reset and the gage works.

terminal.summary: CB77 tripped — reset, gage restored

el-t4.text: A critical gage (oil pressure, water temp, brake air, or volts) does not work, so the BEFORE checks (PMCS items 12, 14, 16, 17) cannot be verified. Notify Unit Maintenance (e7-e12).

terminal.summary: Critical gage inoperative — needs maintenance

el-t5.text: Speedometer or tachometer does not operate. Notify Unit Maintenance (e11/e13).

terminal.summary: Speedometer/tachometer inoperative — needs maintenance

el-q7.text: Remove the PDP cover (para 3-13a). Is the breaker for that light tripped? (CB78 headlights, CB76 turn signals/stoplights, CB80 taillights, CB71 hazard/turn flasher)

el-a4.actionText: Light switch OFF, push the breaker in, light switch back on (para 2-21c). Check whether it trips again. Install the PDP cover (para 3-13b).

options.label: No, or the breaker trips again

el-t8.text: Light circuit breaker was tripped; reset and lights work.

terminal.summary: Light circuit breaker reset — lights restored

el-t7.text: One or more headlights, turn signals, taillights, or stoplights are not operational — NMC (PMCS item 40). Notify Unit Maintenance.

terminal.summary: Headlight/turn signal/taillight/stoplight inoperative — NMC

el-t9.text: Marker or blackout light inoperative. Notify Unit Maintenance (e41-e51). Not an NMC criterion in PMCS item 40.

terminal.summary: Marker/blackout light inoperative — needs maintenance

el-q8.text: Open the battery box (para 3-8a). Are the battery cables damaged or the cables/terminal posts corroded, or are the cable clamps loose?

el-t11.text: Do not clean or tighten battery cables yourself — notify Unit Maintenance (e86). Loose battery cable clamps are NMC (PMCS item 48).

terminal.summary: Battery cables/posts corroded, damaged, or loose — NMC

el-q9.text: Check the battery fluid level (para 3-8b). Is it low, or is the fluid gassing (boiling)?

el-t12.text: Battery fluid low or gassing — notify Unit Maintenance (e86, PMCS item 48c). Close the battery box (para 3-8c).

terminal.summary: Battery fluid low/gassing — notify Unit Maintenance

el-q10.text: Raise the cab (para 2-22a). Are the alternator belts loose or damaged?

el-t13.text: Alternator belts loose or damaged — notify Unit Maintenance (e86). Excessive belt play or cracks/frays beyond limits are NMC (PMCS item 60).

terminal.summary: Alternator belt loose/damaged — NMC

el-q11.text: Lower the cab. With the engine running, does the VOLTS gage read 26-30 volts?

el-t14.text: VOLTS gage outside 26-30 volts is NMC (PMCS item 17). Notify Unit Maintenance.

terminal.summary: Charging system out of range (VOLTS gage) — NMC

el-t15.text: Electrical system does not maintain a charge but voltage is in range now. Notify Unit Maintenance (e86).

terminal.summary: Batteries not holding charge — notify Unit Maintenance

el-t10.text: Wiper, washer, or horn inoperative. Check the breaker (CB37 wipers, CB36 horn) if directed; notify Unit Maintenance (e71-e76). PMCS items 11.1 and 39 have no NMC criterion.

terminal.summary: Wiper/washer/horn inoperative — needs maintenance

un-q1.text: What are you hearing or feeling?

options.label: Engine runs rough, misfires, or knocks
Brakes chatter, grind, groan, or squeal

un-q2.text: Is the AIR FILTER RESTRICTION GAUGE in the red (over 25 in.) after pressing reset?

un-a1.actionText: Shut down the engine and service the air filter element (para 3-9). If the element will not clean, notify Unit Maintenance. Restart (para 2-21a or b).

un-q3.text: Does the engine run smoothly now?

un-t1.text: Restricted air filter was the cause; serviced and the engine runs normally.

terminal.summary: Restricted air filter — serviced, engine runs normally

un-q4.text: Raise the cab (para 2-22a). Check the secondary fuel filter, fuel lines, fittings, draincocks, and tank lines for fuel leaks. Any leaks?

un-t2.text: Fuel leak found. Do not operate — notify Unit Maintenance (a13).

terminal.summary: Engine runs rough — fuel leak found, NMC

un-t3.text: Engine misfires, runs rough, or makes unusual noise with no operator-correctable cause. NMC per PMCS item 24. Notify Unit Maintenance.

terminal.summary: Engine rough running/misfire/unusual noise — NMC

un-q5.text: Is the AIR FILTER RESTRICTION GAUGE in the red after pressing reset?

un-a2.actionText: Shut down and service the air filter element (para 3-9). If it will not clean, notify Unit Maintenance. Restart and check idle.

un-q6.text: Does the engine hold idle now?

un-t4.text: Restricted air filter caused stalling; serviced and the engine holds idle.

terminal.summary: Restricted air filter — serviced, engine holds idle

un-q7.text: Check the air particle restriction hose, and (cab raised) the air cleaner-to-turbocharger pipe and hose. Are any kinked or damaged?

un-t5.text: Kinked or damaged air intake pipe/hose. Notify Unit Maintenance (a4).

terminal.summary: Engine stalls — damaged/kinked air intake hose, needs maintenance

un-t6.text: Engine stalls at low RPM with no operator-correctable cause. Notify Unit Maintenance (a4).

terminal.summary: Engine stalls at low RPM — needs maintenance

un-q8.text: Is the AIR FILTER RESTRICTION GAUGE in the red after pressing reset?

un-a3.actionText: Shut down and service the air filter element (para 3-9). If it will not clean, notify Unit Maintenance. Restart and check vibration.

un-q8a.text: Is the vibration back to normal?

un-t7.text: Restricted air filter caused vibration; serviced.

terminal.summary: Restricted air filter — serviced, vibration normal

un-q9.text: Raise the cab (para 2-22a). Is the vibration damper damaged, or are its bolts loose or missing?

un-t17.text: Vibration damper damaged or bolts loose/missing. Do not operate — notify Unit Maintenance (a6).

terminal.summary: Vibration damper damaged/loose — needs maintenance

un-t18.text: Engine still vibrates too much. Notify Unit Maintenance (a6).

terminal.summary: Excessive engine vibration — needs maintenance

un-t8.text: Exhaust system unusually noisy or vibrates excessively. Notify Unit Maintenance (c1).

terminal.summary: Noisy/vibrating exhaust — needs maintenance

un-t9.text: Exhaust fumes in the cab — carbon monoxide can kill. Stop, ventilate the cab, and notify Unit Maintenance (c2). Do not operate.

terminal.summary: Exhaust fumes in cab — NMC, safety hazard

un-q10.text: With the engine at normal operating temperature, check the TRANSMISSION OIL DIPSTICK (PMCS item 35). What do you find?

options.label: Over HOT FULL, discolored, or milky

un-a4.actionText: Add transmission oil to between HOT ADD and HOT FULL (Appendix F).

un-q11.text: Is the transmission still unusually noisy?

un-t10.text: Transmission oil over HOT FULL, discolored, or milky — NMC (PMCS item 35). Notify Unit Maintenance.

terminal.summary: Transmission oil overfull/contaminated — NMC

un-t11.text: Transmission is unusually noisy when operating. Notify Unit Maintenance (f2).

terminal.summary: Transmission noise — needs maintenance

un-t12.text: Transmission oil was low; added oil and the noise stopped.

terminal.summary: Low transmission oil — added, noise gone

un-q12.text: Check the drive shafts for loose hardware (PMCS item 50d). Is any hardware loose?

un-t13.text: Loose drive shaft hardware is NMC (PMCS item 50d). Notify Unit Maintenance.

terminal.summary: Loose drive shaft hardware — NMC

un-t19.text: Propeller shaft or U-joint unusually noisy. Notify Unit Maintenance (g1).

terminal.summary: Drive shaft/U-joint noise — needs maintenance

un-t14.text: Axle differential noisy. Notify Unit Maintenance (n1).

terminal.summary: Axle differential noise — needs maintenance

un-t15.text: Noisy air compressor operation. Notify Unit Maintenance (j6).

terminal.summary: Air compressor noise — needs maintenance

un-t16.text: Unusual brake noise — notify Unit Maintenance (PMCS item 28c). If the brakes also fail to stop the vehicle or pull to one side, use the Brake Issue tree (NMC).

terminal.summary: Brake noise — needs maintenance

oh-a1.text: Stop and let the engine cool
oh-a1.actionText: Stop in a safe place and shut down. WARNING: use extreme care removing the coolant fill cap if the temperature gage reads above 180°F (82°C); release pressure first. Hot coolant/steam can burn you.

oh-q2.text: Check the coolant level at the radiator overflow tank sightglasses. Is it low?

oh-a2.actionText: Add coolant as required (Appendix F) to between the upper and lower sightglass.

oh-q3.text: Is the radiator cap leaking or damaged?

oh-t1.text: Radiator cap leaking or damaged. Notify Unit Maintenance (d1).

terminal.summary: Engine overheats — radiator cap leaking/damaged

oh-q4.text: Are the radiator overflow tank or hoses leaking or damaged?

oh-t2.text: Overflow tank or hoses leaking/damaged. Notify Unit Maintenance (d1).

terminal.summary: Engine overheats — overflow tank/hose leak or damage

oh-q5.text: Raise the cab (para 2-22a). Are the radiator fins obstructed (mud, debris)?

oh-a3.text: Remove debris from the radiator fins
oh-a3.actionText: Clear the debris from the outside of the radiator core without bending the fins.

oh-q6.text: Check the radiator hoses and hose connections for leakage. What do you find?

oh-t3.text: Damaged radiator hose. Notify Unit Maintenance (d1).

terminal.summary: Engine overheats — damaged radiator hose

oh-q7.text: Lower the cab (para 2-22b), start the engine, and monitor. Does the WATER TEMP gage stay below the red zone with the high engine temperature indicator off?

oh-t4.text: Operator corrections (coolant added / fins cleared / connection tightened) resolved the overheating. Monitor the WATER TEMP gage.

terminal.summary: Overheating corrected at operator level — monitor temperature

oh-t5.text: Engine continues to overheat. WATER TEMP in the red with the indicator on is NMC (PMCS item 14). Notify Unit Maintenance.

terminal.summary: Engine overheats — NMC, needs maintenance

options.label: Low oil pressure (gage under 15 psi or indicator stays on)
Oil over FULL, milky, or discolored / coolant in oil

op-t1.text: Engine oil over the FULL line, discolored, or milky is NMC (PMCS item 34); coolant in oil — notify Unit Maintenance (a7).

terminal.summary: Engine oil overfull/milky/contaminated — NMC

op-q2.text: Shut down. Raise the cab (para 2-22a) and check the dipstick (PMCS item 34). What is the level?

op-a1.actionText: WARNING: the dipstick is near the starter solenoid (24 VDC). Add engine oil (Appendix F) to between ADD and FULL. Do not overfill.

op-q3.text: Is the oil contaminated (milky, discolored, fuel smell)?

op-q4.text: Lower the cab (para 2-22b) and restart. Is OIL PRESS 15 psi or more and the indicator off?

op-t2.text: Oil pressure normal after the oil level was corrected/verified. Monitor the OIL PRESS gage.

terminal.summary: Low oil level corrected — oil pressure normal

op-t3.text: Engine oil pressure still low — NMC (PMCS item 12). Shut down and notify Unit Maintenance.

terminal.summary: Low engine oil pressure — NMC

op-q6.text: Raise the cab and check the dipstick. What is the level?

op-a2.actionText: Add engine oil to between ADD and FULL (Appendix F).

op-q7.text: Check oil lines, the engine block, and the oil filter for leaks. What class (para 2-14)?

op-t4.text: Class III oil leak — NMC. Notify Unit Maintenance (a8).

terminal.summary: Excessive oil consumption — Class III oil leak, NMC

op-t5.text: Class II oil leak: report to Unit Maintenance (a8); operation is allowed — check the oil level often.

terminal.summary: Excessive oil consumption — Class II leak, notify Unit Maintenance

op-t6.text: Oil consumption still excessive with no visible leak. Notify Unit Maintenance (a8).

terminal.summary: Excessive oil consumption — needs maintenance

op-q8.text: Raise the cab and check the dipstick (a14). What is the level?

op-a3.actionText: Add engine oil to between ADD and FULL (Appendix F). Lower the cab (para 2-22b) and run the engine.

op-q9.text: Is blue exhaust smoke still seen?

op-t7.text: Blue exhaust smoke persists. Excessive exhaust smoke is NMC (PMCS item 24). Notify Unit Maintenance (a14).

terminal.summary: Blue exhaust smoke — NMC, needs maintenance

op-t8.text: Oil level was low; added oil and blue smoke stopped.

terminal.summary: Low oil — added, blue smoke stopped

es-t1.text: Engine overspeeds on start — shut it down. Notify Unit Maintenance (a5).

terminal.summary: Engine overspeeds on start — NMC

es-q2.text: Is the AIR FILTER RESTRICTION GAUGE in the red after pressing reset?

es-a1.actionText: Shut down and service the air filter element (para 3-9). If it will not clean, notify Unit Maintenance. Restart.

es-t2.text: Restricted air filter caused the smoke; serviced and smoke cleared.

terminal.summary: Restricted air filter — serviced, smoke cleared

es-q4.text: Check the air particle restriction hose and (cab raised) the air cleaner-to-turbocharger pipe and hose. Kinked or damaged?

es-t3.text: Damaged or kinked air intake pipe/hose. Notify Unit Maintenance (a10).

terminal.summary: Black/gray smoke — damaged air intake hose, NMC

es-t4.text: Excessive black or gray smoke persists — NMC (PMCS item 24). Notify Unit Maintenance (a10).

terminal.summary: Excessive black/gray exhaust smoke — NMC

es-q5.text: Is the AIR FILTER RESTRICTION GAUGE in the red after pressing reset?

es-a2.actionText: Shut down and service the air filter element (para 3-9). Restart.

es-t6.text: Restricted air filter caused white smoke; serviced.

terminal.summary: Restricted air filter — serviced, white smoke cleared

es-t5.text: White exhaust smoke persists — excessive smoke is NMC (PMCS item 24). Notify Unit Maintenance (a11).

terminal.summary: White exhaust smoke — NMC

es-q7.text: Raise the cab and check the engine oil dipstick (a14). What is the level?

es-a3.actionText: Add engine oil (Appendix F) to between ADD and FULL. Lower the cab and run the engine.

es-t7.text: Engine oil over FULL — NMC (PMCS item 34). Notify Unit Maintenance.

terminal.summary: Engine oil overfull — NMC

es-t8.text: Blue exhaust smoke persists — NMC (PMCS item 24). Notify Unit Maintenance (a14).

terminal.summary: Blue exhaust smoke — NMC

es-t9.text: Low oil was the cause; added oil and blue smoke stopped.

terminal.summary: Low oil — added, blue smoke stopped

es-q9.text: Is there contamination (water, sediment) in the fuel tank? (a15 step 1)

es-t10.text: Fuel tank contamination. Notify Unit Maintenance (a15).

terminal.summary: Low power — fuel contamination, NMC

es-q10.text: Raise the cab and check the engine oil level. What is it?

es-q11.text: Is the AIR FILTER RESTRICTION GAUGE in the red after pressing reset?

es-a4.actionText: Service the air filter element (para 3-9). If it will not clean, notify Unit Maintenance.

es-q12.text: Are the air particle restriction hose or the air cleaner-to-turbocharger pipe/hose kinked or damaged?

es-t11.text: Damaged/kinked air intake pipe or hose. Notify Unit Maintenance (a15).

terminal.summary: Low power — damaged air intake hose, NMC

es-q13.text: Lower the cab and road test. Does the engine now have normal power?

es-t12.text: Power restored after operator checks (oil added and/or air filter serviced).

terminal.summary: Low power corrected at operator level

es-t13.text: Engine has low power after operator checks. Notify Unit Maintenance (a15).

terminal.summary: Low engine power — needs maintenance

bi-q1.text: What is the brake problem? (LMTV service and parking brakes are air-operated.)

options.label: Brakes do not stop the vehicle / braking distance too long
Vehicle pulls to one side, brakes unevenly, or grabs
Front or rear brakes do not apply
Vehicle moves with SYSTEM PARK on / parking brakes do not apply
BRAKE AIR gage under 65 psi, BRAKE AIR light, or alarm
Air leak when brakes are applied

bi-t1.text: Either brake air gage below 65 psi, a BRAKE AIR indicator on, or the audible alarm is NMC (PMCS item 16). Notify Unit Maintenance (j1).

terminal.summary: Low brake air pressure — NMC

bi-t2.text: Brake system loses air when service brakes are applied. Notify Unit Maintenance (i9).

terminal.summary: Brake system loses air when applied — NMC

bi-t3.text: Unusual noises when braking — notify Unit Maintenance (PMCS item 28c). Noise alone is not an NMC criterion.

terminal.summary: Brake noise — needs maintenance

bi-q2.text: Start the engine and idle until FRONT BRAKE AIR and REAR BRAKE AIR read 120 psi (827 kPa), then shut down. Do both gages reach 120 psi?

bi-t4.text: Service brakes do not stop the vehicle — NMC (PMCS item 28a). Notify Unit Maintenance (i1).

terminal.summary: Service brakes do not stop vehicle — NMC

bi-t5.text: Air tanks do not reach 120 psi. Notify Unit Maintenance (i1/j1). Do not operate.

terminal.summary: Brakes weak — air system does not build 120 psi, NMC

bi-q3.text: Start the engine and idle until FRONT BRAKE AIR and REAR BRAKE AIR read 120 psi (827 kPa), then shut down. Do both gages reach 120 psi?

bi-t6.text: Vehicle pulls to one side when service brakes are applied — NMC (PMCS item 28b). Notify Unit Maintenance (i5).

terminal.summary: Brakes pull to one side — NMC

bi-q4.text: Start the engine and idle until FRONT BRAKE AIR and REAR BRAKE AIR read 120 psi (827 kPa), then shut down. Do both gages reach 120 psi?

bi-t7.text: Front or rear brakes do not apply. Notify Unit Maintenance (i2/i6).

terminal.summary: Front/rear brakes do not apply — NMC

bi-q5.text: Do the FRONT and REAR BRAKE AIR gages read 65-120 psi?

bi-t8.text: Vehicle moves with SYSTEM PARK on / parking brakes do not apply — NMC (PMCS item 19). Notify Unit Maintenance (i8).

terminal.summary: Parking brake does not hold — NMC

bi-q6.text: Start the engine and idle until FRONT BRAKE AIR and REAR BRAKE AIR read 120 psi (827 kPa), then shut down. Do both gages reach 120 psi?

bi-t9.text: Parking brake(s) will not release with full air pressure. Notify Unit Maintenance (i3).

terminal.summary: Parking brakes will not release — NMC

bi-q7.text: Check tire inflation and damage (PMCS item 38). Are tires improperly inflated?

bi-a1.actionText: Start the engine and select the correct CTIS mode (para 2-23). Shut down and check inflation. If tires are damaged, notify Unit Maintenance.

bi-q8.text: Front brakes only: check the front gladhands for damage, air leaks, and obstructions; clean if obstructed, lubricate coupler seals, and reinstall dummy couplings (i4 step 2). Do the brakes still overheat?

bi-t10.text: Overheating stopped after correcting tire inflation / servicing gladhands.

terminal.summary: Brake overheating corrected (tire pressure/gladhands)

bi-t11.text: Brakes still overheat or do not release. Notify Unit Maintenance (i4/i7).

terminal.summary: Brakes overheat/drag — needs maintenance

options.label: TEPSS beeps for 8 seconds, TPSS shows "--", or it will not shift
A gear range does not work, or a service message will not reset
Shift selector is dark / does not light
Transmission oil over HOT FULL, discolored, or milky

tr-t1.text: Notify Unit Maintenance (f1/f3). A gear range that does not operate is NMC (PMCS item 20).

terminal.summary: Transmission will not shift / TPSS fault — NMC

tr-t2.text: One gear range does not operate properly, or a service message cannot be reset — NMC (PMCS item 20).

terminal.summary: Gear range inoperative / service message — NMC

tr-a1.actionText: Master power OFF. Remove the PDP cover (para 3-13a). WTEC II: check CB35 and CB79. WTEC III: check CB43 and CB79. Push any tripped breaker in. Master power ON and check if it trips again. Install the PDP cover (para 3-13b).

tr-q2.text: Does the shift selector light up and work now?

options.label: No, or a breaker tripped again

tr-t4.text: Shift selector breaker was tripped; reset and the selector works.

terminal.summary: Shift selector breaker reset — selector works

tr-t5.text: Shift selector does not illuminate/operate. Notify Unit Maintenance (f1a/f4).

terminal.summary: Shift selector inoperative — NMC

tr-t3.text: Transmission oil over HOT FULL, discolored, or milky — NMC (PMCS item 35). Notify Unit Maintenance.

terminal.summary: Transmission oil overfull/contaminated — NMC

options.label: Class III — drops drip from the item

tr-t7.text: Class III transmission oil leak — NMC. Notify Unit Maintenance.

terminal.summary: Class III transmission oil leak — NMC

tr-t8.text: Class I/II leakage is allowed; check the transmission oil level often (PMCS item 35) and report it.

terminal.summary: Class I/II transmission oil leak — monitor and report

tr-q4.text: Engine at operating temperature: check the TRANSMISSION OIL DIPSTICK. What do you find?

options.label: Over HOT FULL, discolored, or milky

tr-a2.actionText: Add oil to between HOT ADD and HOT FULL (Appendix F).

tr-q5.text: Is the transmission still unusually noisy?

tr-t9.text: Transmission unusually noisy when operating. Notify Unit Maintenance (f2).

terminal.summary: Transmission noise — needs maintenance

tr-t10.text: Transmission oil was low; added and the noise stopped.

terminal.summary: Low transmission oil — added, noise gone

tr-t6.text: Transmission over-temperature: a warning light the operator cannot correct is NMC (PMCS item 23). Stop safely and notify Unit Maintenance.

terminal.summary: Transmission temperature warning — NMC

options.label: Excessive play when turning the wheel
No response when turning the wheel
Wanders, pulls to one side, or shimmies

st-t1.text: No response when turning the steering wheel. Do not operate — NMC (PMCS item 27). Notify Unit Maintenance (p4).

terminal.summary: Steering unresponsive — NMC

st-t2.text: Unusual steering noise without binding — notify Unit Maintenance (PMCS item 27).

terminal.summary: Steering noise — needs maintenance

st-q2.text: Raise the cab (para 2-22a). Check the power steering reservoir dipstick (CAUTION: do not overfill). What is the level?

st-a1.actionText: Add oil to the full mark (Appendix F). Do not overfill.

st-t3.text: Power steering oil over the full mark — notify Unit Maintenance (p1/s1). With hard steering or play, the vehicle is NMC (PMCS item 27).

terminal.summary: Power steering overfull with steering fault — NMC

st-q3.text: Check the steering hydraulic lines and fittings. Any Class III leaks?

st-t4.text: Class III leak in the steering hydraulic system — NMC. Notify Unit Maintenance (s1).

terminal.summary: Steering hydraulic Class III leak — NMC

st-q4.text: Lower the cab. Check tire pressures for the CTIS setting (HWY 55, X-C 33, SAND 20, EMER 14 psi). Do they match?

st-t5.text: Tire pressures do not match the CTIS setting — notify Unit Maintenance (p1). Steering that binds or is unresponsive is NMC (PMCS item 27).

terminal.summary: Hard steering — tire pressures out of spec, needs maintenance

st-q5.text: Is the steering still hard or does it still have excessive play?

st-t6.text: Power steering oil was low; topped off and steering is normal. Check the reservoir for leaks at the next weekly PMCS (item 64).

terminal.summary: Low power steering oil — added, steering normal

st-t7.text: Steering still hard or has excessive play — NMC (PMCS item 27: binds or unresponsive). Notify Unit Maintenance (p1/p3).

terminal.summary: Hard steering/excessive play — NMC

st-q6.text: Check the wheel studs and lug nuts for obvious looseness (p2). What do you find?

options.label: Two or more nuts/studs missing, loose, or broken on one wheel

st-t8.text: Two or more lug nuts/studs missing, loose, or broken on the same wheel — NMC (PMCS item 46c). Notify Unit Maintenance.

terminal.summary: Lug nuts/studs missing or broken — NMC

st-q7.text: Check tire pressures for the CTIS setting. Do they match? (If you tightened a nut, Unit Maintenance must torque it to 415-475 lb-ft.)

st-t9.text: Vehicle wanders, pulls, or shimmies with correct pressures and tight lug nuts. Check brakes for pulling (Brake Issue tree, i5) and notify Unit Maintenance (q1).

terminal.summary: Vehicle wanders/pulls/shimmies — needs maintenance

st-t10.text: Tire pressures do not match the CTIS setting — notify Unit Maintenance (p2).

terminal.summary: Wander/pull — tire pressures out of spec, needs maintenance

fs-q1.text: What is the fuel system problem?

options.label: Water in the fuel/water separator bowl
Fuel cap loose/damaged or fuel strainer clogged/damaged/missing
Ether starting aid does not work

fs-q2.text: Raise the cab (para 2-22a). Check the secondary fuel filter, fuel lines, fittings, draincocks, tank lines, and tank for leaks. What do you find?

fs-t4.text: Class III fuel leak — NMC, fire hazard. Notify Unit Maintenance.

terminal.summary: Class III fuel leak — NMC

fs-t5.text: Fuel leak found — notify Unit Maintenance (b3). Class I/II leakage is allowed (para 2-14); keep it away from heat and check it often.

terminal.summary: Class I/II fuel leak — report to Unit Maintenance

fs-t6.text: Fuel consumption still too high with no leaks. Notify Unit Maintenance (b3).

terminal.summary: High fuel consumption — needs maintenance

fs-a1.actionText: WARNING: no smoking or sparks. Turn the knurled nut left to open the drain valve and drain into a container until only pure fuel comes out; close the valve by turning the nut right (PMCS item 32b). Excessive condensation in fuel: see e91.

fs-t7.text: Water drained from the fuel/water separator.

terminal.summary: Water drained from fuel/water separator

fs-t1.text: Fuel cap or strainer damaged/missing — notify Unit Maintenance (PMCS item 58; no NMC criterion unless there is a Class III leak).

terminal.summary: Fuel cap/strainer damaged or missing — needs maintenance

fs-t2.text: Ether starting aid does not operate. Notify Unit Maintenance (b2).

terminal.summary: Ether starting aid inoperative — needs maintenance

fs-t3.text: Sticking accelerator pedal — do not operate. Notify Unit Maintenance (b4).

terminal.summary: Accelerator pedal sticks — NMC, safety

cs-q1.text: What did you find? (For a hot engine, use Engine Overheats.)

cs-t1.text: Oil in the cooling system — NMC (PMCS item 3b). Notify Unit Maintenance (d2).

terminal.summary: Oil in cooling system — NMC

cs-a1.actionText: WARNING: release reservoir pressure before removing the cap; use extreme care above 180°F (82°C). Add coolant (Appendix F) to between the upper and lower sightglass with the engine not running.

cs-q1a.text: Does the level hold, with no visible leaks?

options.label: No — level drops or a leak is visible

cs-t2.text: Coolant was low; topped off and the level holds.

terminal.summary: Coolant low — topped off, level holds

cs-q2.text: Is the radiator cap leaking or damaged? (d3 step 1)

cs-t3.text: Radiator cap leaking or damaged. Notify Unit Maintenance (d3).

terminal.summary: Coolant loss — radiator cap leaking/damaged

cs-q3.text: Are the radiator overflow tank or hoses leaking or damaged?

cs-t4.text: Overflow tank or hoses leaking/damaged. Notify Unit Maintenance (d3). A Class III leak is NMC (PMCS item 62).

terminal.summary: Coolant loss — overflow tank/hose leak

cs-q4.text: Raise the cab (para 2-22a). Check all hoses and connections for leakage. What do you find?

cs-a2.actionText: Tighten the loose clamp/connection. Clear any debris from the radiator fins. Lower the cab (para 2-22b) and monitor the coolant level.

cs-t5.text: Damaged coolant hose. Notify Unit Maintenance (d3).

terminal.summary: Coolant loss — damaged hose

cs-t6.text: Coolant loss continues with no operator-correctable cause. Notify Unit Maintenance (d3).

terminal.summary: Coolant loss — needs maintenance

cs-t7.text: Loose hose connection tightened; coolant loss stopped.

terminal.summary: Loose coolant hose connection — tightened
